scope: Cold-to-warm historical-input prototype, not certified reproduction of FGH Figures 1 and 2

inputs.heating_source: GHF Eqs12-13, p178: n_fast*(3.2e-19*nHI+4.1e-17*ne), plus direct electron heating
inputs.H_ionization_triangle: GHF p178: threshold13.6eV, peak1.2e-16cm2 at50eV, zero at300eV
inputs.H_excitation: Infer sigma(20eV) from rounded Eq13 minus the explicit H ionization contribution in Eq12. Assume a linear ramp from10.2 to20eV. Test zero beyond20 versus indefinite linear continuation; neither tail is recovered historical data.
inputs.abundances: config-cold.json: Field1968 baseline and FGH Letter depletion divisors, not mixed with GHF cases

limitations: Lyman-alpha near-threshold ramp is an assumption: the actual Fite et al. data and Goldsmith1969 thesis fit have not been recovered. Tail sensitivity cannot validate this slope or the inferred20eV normalization.
Thermal He excitation and ionization omitted; low warm-branch temperatures motivate but do not validate this approximation. No extension beyond12000K.
Hjellming excited-state kinetic recombination energy is baseline. An explicit2/3 multiplier tests the unresolved GHF Eq17 energy convention; this is not an uncertainty interval.
HeI recombination approximated by hydrogen. Metal cooling uses the low-density sum, whole elemental populations per transition and available collider channels only; no level statistical equilibrium.
H/He charge neutrality follows the printed GHF closure without metal-donor electrons. Pressure excludes trace nuclei and superthermal electrons.
Sign-change root scans can miss tangent roots; doubled scans test numerical robustness but cannot certify completeness.
Pressure turning points demonstrate the prototype S-curve only. No conductive saturation pressure, Maxwell equal-area construction, or full ionization-dependent stability analysis is inferred.

A96-point sparse digitized comparison is available in compare.py. Historical agreement remains unvalidated, and further rate recovery is deferred. Numerical conservation does not establish historical accuracy.
